notes: Thirty-three people in their Scene 1 seats, with Scene 4A's three moves kept exactly; Eleazar at the wall (27.7, 2.8) with his hand on the loose stone, Jotham at the north gatepost (28.25, 1.95), Tirzah pressed close to her father (1.15, −0.62).
The small fire burns at the shared anchor fire_sc11_sc16 (3.2, −0.4), between the ledge and groups A and B; Scene 16 uses the same fire, burning low.
Six clay lamps are in hands across the groups (people 7, 11, 16, 22, 27 and 30), each drawn just in front of its holder.
One unbroken take of eight windows with two hidden stitches, the smoothed wax of Jotham's tablet and the flames of the fire.

Jotham's 'Look at the publican' turns the camera and walks it through the gate and 24 m down the open ground to the fire at about 2.5 m/s, the reverse of Scene 1's W14 crossing and the gap Jotham crosses himself in Scene 16.
From the mouth of the gate the north pier hides the loose stone, so Scene 11 keeps Eleazar in profile against the grove and leaves his hand on the stone to Scenes 4A and 16.
Dusk afterglow from about 140°, lower and redder than Scene 1; the Pharisees stand at the edge of the light and the faces at the ledge take the firelight.
The take ends behind the teacher's right shoulder, near Scene 1's S10, with Hezron and Tirzah, the fire and the gate in one frame for 'to Hezron now as much as to the gate'.
Everyone stays seated in Scene 11; the child sits where Scene 1's lizard chase ended.
